title: Unveiling the dual Z-scheme g-C 3 N 4 /Sm 2 O 3 /Gd 2 O 3  heterostructure for efficient photocatalytic detoxification of tetracycline antibiotics with reduced phytotoxicity
content: The pervasive occurrence of antibiotic residues in aquatic systems necessitates transformative remediation strategies to safeguard public health and ecosystems. In this work, we report the rational design of a dual Z-scheme heterostructure photocatalyst for the efficient degradation of tetracycline and doxycycline from aquatic environments. A series of ternary composites were fabricated by embedding different wt% of binary Sm2O3/Gd2O3 (S1) into the g-C3N4 matrix via a hydrothermal/ultrasonication-assisted approach, followed by comprehensive physicochemical characterization to elucidate the impact of binary oxides in modulating the g-C3N4 framework. Morphological investigation revealed the in situ growth of binary oxides within the layered stacking of g-C3N4, while radical scavenging and Mott–Schottky plots corroborated the dual Z-scheme charge transfer pathway. The optimized CS-10 composite exhibited superior photoactivity, achieving 93% tetracycline and 91% doxycycline removal (50 mg L−1) within 60 minutes of light irradiation, with recyclability sustained over four cycles. Phytotoxicity assays using Vigna radiata also showed enhanced root and shoot growth in the CS-10 composite, indicating reduced effluent toxicity and validating environmental applicability. Overall, these findings establish the CS-10 catalyst as a robust and scalable photocatalyst with significant potential for mitigating antibiotic contamination in pollutant-laden matrices.
